archetypes.name: code-robustness
archetypes.rationale: File I/O with error suppression, path-key matching between manifest and collector records, and cleanup interactions all warrant edge-case scrutiny.
archetypes.prompt_body: Examine `write_reviewer_status_tsv` in `python/plan_review_round.py`: the function joins manifest `output` paths to collector `REVIEWER_FILE` paths as absolute string keys -- verify these are guaranteed to match (same base, same normalization) across the collector-record pipeline. Check what `_valid_manifest_slot_row` (called at the manifest filtering step) accepts and rejects; determine whether a row with a missing or empty `output` field can pass validation and silently produce a wrong `skipped` status instead of being excluded. Audit the two `contextlib.suppress(OSError)` call sites -- one inside `execute_round` and one in `_run_round_body` in `plan_review.py` -- to confirm they do not swallow failures that should propagate, and that `round_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)` inside the function cannot race with `_clean_round_dir` called earlier in the subprocess branch. Also verify that the symlink guard (`if out.is_symlink(): return None`) before `out.write_text(...)` meaningfully closes the TOCTOU window on the target platform. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: architecture
archetypes.rationale: The fix introduces a new cross-module public function and two asymmetric call sites; verifying their contract symmetry and data-availability ordering is important.
archetypes.prompt_body: Review the producer/consumer contract for `reviewer-status.tsv` as established by this diff: `write_reviewer_status_tsv` is now a public function in `plan_review_round.py` called from both `execute_round` (primary, always fires) and from `_run_round_body` in `plan_review.py` (subprocess fallback, fires only when the file is absent). Verify that both call sites fire with `collector-results.env` and `plan-review-slots.ndjson` already written at the `design/` root -- confirm neither file lives in the round subdirectory that `_clean_round_dir` clears before the subprocess launch. Check that the copy-to-`latest-reviewer-status.tsv` logic downstream of each call site still executes after the producer runs (not before), so the copy guard `if round_status.is_file()` is satisfied in both paths. Assess whether exposing `write_reviewer_status_tsv` as a public cross-module function is the right abstraction boundary or whether the caller should be restructured. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
